claims.text: Bones: femur, patella, tibia, fibula, tarsal bones, metatarsal bones and phalanges.
claims.quote: These are the femur, patella, tibia, fibula, tarsal bones, metatarsal bones, and phalanges

claims.text: Foot: seven tarsal bones form the posterior foot and five metatarsals the mid-foot.
claims.quote: The posterior portion of the foot is formed by a group of seven bones, each of which is known as a tarsal bone, whereas the mid-foot contains five elongated bones, each of which is a metatarsal bone.

claims.text: Leg: the tibia is the larger, weight-bearing medial bone; the fibula is the thin lateral bone.
claims.quote: The tibia is the larger, weight-bearing bone located on the medial side of the leg, and the fibula is the thin bone of the lateral leg.

claims.text: Hip joint: the head of the femur articulates with the acetabulum of the hip bone.
claims.quote: The rounded, proximal end is the head of the femur, which articulates with the acetabulum of the hip bone to form the hip joint.

claims.text: Femoral head blood supply: the ligament of the head of the femur gives little support but carries an important artery to the femoral head.
claims.quote: This ligament spans the femur and acetabulum, but is weak and provides little support for the hip joint. It does, however, carry an important artery that supplies the head of the femur.

claims.text: Femoral neck: the narrowed region below the head; a common site of femur fractures.
claims.quote: The narrowed region below the head is the neck of the femur. This is a common area for fractures of the femur.

claims.text: Knee: the lateral and medial femoral condyles articulate with the tibia to form the knee joint.
claims.quote: The lateral and medial condyles articulate with the tibia to form the knee joint.

claims.text: Patella: articulates only with the distal femur.
claims.quote: The patella only articulates with the distal end of the femur.
